newsitem.title: USA: Strong economy boosts Mass. tax revenues - paper.
newsitem.headline: Strong economy boosts Mass. tax revenues - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Revenue Commissioner Mitchell Adams reported the state took in $1.4 billion in April -- almost 40 percent more that it collected for the same month a year earlier, Boston Globe reported Friday.
The tax bonus all but guarantees the state will end the fiscal year in June with a substantial budget surplus -- about $400 million -- unnamed tax specialists told the Globe.

Much of the extra money is likely to go into an expanded "rainy day" fund for the future and legislative sources told the Globe that some of the money could be used to pay down on some of Massachusetts' substantial debts.
House Speaker Thomas Finneran has made no secret of the fact that he would like to see the state pay off some of its debt.
Officals at the Revenue Commissiion were not immediately available for comment.
